public_rationale: Acher's report available May 25, 2025 documents substantive illegal moves by o3, separately identifying two notation-related exceptions [e1]. It also records o3 incorrectly reconstructing a chess position and rejecting a legal opponent move [e1]. This supports the claim that o3 remained vulnerable to failures in maintaining game state and applying rules [e1]. The same report includes competent legal play, so the finding concerns vulnerability rather than failure in every game [e2]. Support is limited to this behavioral reading of the claimed world-model problem [e1, e2].
limitations: The chess tests do not establish that o3 lacks internal world models or identify the cause of its errors [e1, e2].
They do not test the y/z tic-tac-toe variant or settle the hedged comparison with Grok [e1, e2].
Individual test dates are unspecified, and inconsistent sample descriptions prevent a reliable aggregate failure-rate estimate [e1, e2].

our_interpretation: The ordinary behavioral reading is that o3 can fail to maintain an accurate game state or apply its rules consistently. Losing a game alone would not establish this.
The comparison with Grok is a concession, not a conditional forecast.
The observation concerns the contemporary o3 release through the post date. I use its release-to-post interval because no observation window is specified.
Behavioral failures can establish vulnerability without establishing the complete absence of internal world representations.

criteria.contradiction_condition: The alleged state and rule failures are shown to be evaluation artifacts, and sufficiently broad comparable testing demonstrates reliable state tracking under the challenged conditions.

evidence.explanation: Acher describes substantive o3 rule violations and an incorrect reconstruction of a game state. He separately identifies two notation-related cases, so the substantive finding does not depend on counting those as failures.
The same report includes competent legal play and a winning o3-high game. This limits any interpretation that o3 invariably fails or has no chess competence, but does not contradict vulnerability.
